changes.before:
FileCompresser's current extraction tool is designed for ZIP files. It does not support every archive format.

The current workflow does not support RAR or 7z files. Encrypted archives, split archives, and ZIP64 archives are also not supported.

If you receive an archive in one of these formats, you will need a compatible extraction application. Changing the file extension does not convert an unsupported archive into a standard ZIP file.

The maximum supported input size for the ZIP Extractor is 150 MB. Make sure your archive is within this limit before starting the process.

Extraction allows up to 500 entries, 200 MB per file and 500 MB total extracted data. A per-entry or whole-archive expansion ratio above 100:1 is refused. These bounds are separate from the input queue limit.

changes.before:
FileCompresser processes supported ZIP archives directly in your browser. Your selected archive does not need to be uploaded to an external server for extraction, and you do not need to create an account to use the tool.

The input file limit is 150 MB. The general processing queue supports up to 500 files and a combined queue size of up to 300 MB, subject to the tool's archive and extraction limits.

Processing capacity can also depend on your device and browser. Large archives with many files or a high amount of extracted data may require more memory and processing time.

changes.before:
A browser-based file compressor provides a convenient way to manage files without installing additional software. You can open the website, select your files and complete the task using your existing browser.

Other useful features include:

- No account or registration required.
- No software installation.
- No added watermarks.
- Support for multiple file formats.
- Actual file size comparisons.
- Individual and supported batch downloads.
- Automatic selection of the appropriate processing workflow.

The queue supports up to 500 files and 300 MB in total. The maximum individual file size depends on the selected processing tool. Browser memory and device performance can also affect the processing time.

changes.before:
FileCompresser processes GIF files directly on your device. The website loads its media processing engine when needed, and your browser may cache the required code for later use.

The tool accepts GIF files up to 50 MB. It also applies preflight limits of 1,000 frames, a 32-megapixel canvas and 64 million pixels across full-canvas frames.

Long or complex animations can still require significant memory. If processing fails, try a shorter animation or a smaller source file.

The audio engine may need to download the first time you use a media tool. This initial download is around 21 MB and can be cached by your browser for later use. MP3 processing also has a five-minute job limit, so very long recordings may not finish within the available processing time.

The tool supports MP3 files up to 100 MB. If your audio is larger than this limit, you will need to use a smaller source file.

changes.before:
FileCompresser processes supported PDF files directly in your browser. Your selected document does not need to be uploaded to an external server for the optimization process, and you do not need to create an account to use the tool.

The maximum supported PDF file size is 50 MB. The workflow is designed for supported, unsigned, and unencrypted PDF documents. If a file is protected or digitally signed, the tool will not process it.

For important documents, keep a separate original copy. After processing, open the downloaded PDF and check its pages, links, forms, and layout before sharing or replacing the original.
